Apple has just released the RC version of iOS 26.6 along with its accompanying updates. The official release notes from Apple confirm the addition of a feature to prepare your iPhone for iOS 27.

Apple will begin Spotlight indexing work starting with iOS 26.6 to get your iPhone ready for iOS 27

It's unusual for Apple to explicitly mention a future software update in the release notes of a new version.

However, that is exactly what happened today with the release of the iOS 26.6 RC version.

Here are the official release notes for iOS 26.6:

Since the beta revealed virtually no new features, iOS 26.6 is primarily a bug fix and security update, which is what we expected.

Still, the mention of Spotlight indexing work is rather interesting.

When the iOS 27 beta first launched last month, developers noticed that their iPhones were busy with indexing work for extended periods. In many cases, the indexing process took a week or even longer.

As it turns out, Apple doesn't want the public to go through this experience again when iOS 27 rolls out this fall.

Therefore, Apple is getting most of the indexing work done early through iOS 26.6, paving the way for a smoother experience with iOS 27.

So, if you notice your iPhone doing Spotlight indexing work after installing iOS 26.6, there's a good reason for it—the major improvements coming to Siri and Spotlight in iOS 27 will benefit from this groundwork.
